hook.line: At the clinic, nobody says "lie on your back". The doctor tells you which way your face points. You will hear this one the first time someone needs to look at your back or your knee.

examples.es: Estuve de pie todo el día.
examples.en: I was on my feet all day.
My grandmother used to sleep face up.
Do you sleep face up or on your side? (to a friend)

rule:
Spanish names a body position with a short fixed phrase, and there is no article and no "on your" in it:

*boca arriba*: face up, on your back
*boca abajo*: face down, on your stomach
*de rodillas*: kneeling
*de pie*: standing, on your feet
*de lado*: on your side

They follow verbs like *estar*, *dormir*, *acostarse* and *ponerse*. With *ponerse* they say how someone got into the position: *se puso de pie*, he stood up.

English talks about the back or the stomach. Spanish talks about the face: *arriba* is up, *abajo* is down.
smallPrint: Teachers call these adverbial phrases of position. Learn each one as a single block.

readAndPick.es: Estuve de pie todo el día.
options: I was lying down all day.
I was on my feet all day.
I can't sleep on my back.
I can't sleep on my stomach.
My grandmother used to sleep on her back.
My grandmother used to sleep on her stomach.
My grandmother used to sleep on her side.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *arriba* or *abajo*. The doctor wants a patient on their back (formal): Acuéstese boca ___, por favor.
yourTurn.why: Face up, on your back, is *boca arriba*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I was on my feet all day.
yourTurn.answer: Estuve de pie todo el día.
accept: Todo el día estuve de pie.
yourTurn.why: Standing is *de pie*, with no article.

yourTurn.prompt: Say about Vale: She sleeps face down.
yourTurn.why: Face down is *boca abajo*, and *abajo* means down.
*Ponerse de rodillas* says how he got into the position.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal. The doctor says to an older patient: Acuéstate boca arriba.
yourTurn.why: To someone you address as *usted*, the command ends in *-ese*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say you sleep on your stomach, not on your back: Duermo boca arriba.
yourTurn.why: Swap *arriba* for *abajo* to flip the position.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Do you sleep face up or on your side?
yourTurn.why: *De lado* is the third common position, and the question uses *tú*, so *duermes*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estuve en los pies todo el día.
pitfalls.right: Estuve de pie todo el día.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish uses the fixed phrase *de pie* for standing, not a phrase about feet.
Spanish says which way the face points: *boca arriba*, not "on the back".
The phrase starts with *de*, as in *de pie* and *de lado*.

personal: Say how you usually sleep, with *duermo* and *boca arriba*, *boca abajo* or *de lado*.
